question: With a limited classification improvement from extra methods, can the selected binary classifier use its own three training-held prediction panels to decide how much probability is needed to choose the positive class? This preserves the ordinary selected method and uses no extra classifier fits.
method: For each frozen ordinary result, only use held-out predictions of the actually selected members. Combine equal-probability voters as in the source. On each two out of three assessment panels fit a classification cutoff by pooled accuracy over a fixed grid from 0.38 to 0.62 in steps of 0.015, resolving ties toward 0.5. Test each fitted cutoff on the excluded panel. Apply their median at prediction only when the three cutoffs include two on the same side of 0.5, the median differs from 0.5, no held score decreases by more than .003, and pooled held accuracy gains at least .003; otherwise retain the ordinary decision. Row identities and score payload must match the original solves.
study: Five previously completed expanded-ordinary solves at 32-fit budget and five at 48-fit budget, using the exact original members and memoized predictions/model artifacts. Complete all ten threshold decisions and seal query outputs before reading any outside-fold labels for this new procedure. The prior ordinary outer scores are known, these are development replays, and the two five-fold experiments reuse course training rows. No new base fits, course validation, test, H2 or model API.
qualify: For a fresh ordinary-entry integration require at least .003 pooled held improvement within the 48-cap study and a positive gain within the 32-cap study; no individual fold in either set may regress by more than .003. Report exact paired changes and confidence intervals even when the policy declines to change.
